question: A goldsmith uses 110 cm³ of gold to make a wire 1 mm in diameter. He will use this wire to make gold chains of equal lengths. If each chain requires 56 cm length of wire, then how many gold chains can he make? [Use pi=(22)/(7)]
solution:
Given:

A goldsmith uses 110 cm3 of gold to make a wire 1 mm in diameter. He will use this wire to make gold chains of equal lengths. 

Each chain requires 56 cm length of wire.

Concept used:

1. Volume of a cylinder = πR2H (where r = Radius of the base, h = height)

2. 1 cm = 10 mm

Calculation:

Radius of the gold wire = 1/2 = 0.5 mm = 0.05 cm

The volume of each gold chain = π × (0.05)² × 56 = 0.44 cm³

Now, the number of gold chains he can make = 110/0.44 = 250

∴ He can make 250 gold chains.
